Answer: D
Reason: The imaging series demonstrates a rapid progression from initial interstitial opacities to severe bilateral alveolar consolidations, followed by complete resolution in the follow-up X-rays (Figures 5a and 5b). This pattern of fulminant pulmonary involvement with total radiological clearance is characteristic of Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis), distinguishing it from conditions like bacterial pneumonia or crack lung which typically leave residual scarring or have different clinical courses.
